title: CDL Hazmat classes and definitions practice questions
description: Free CDL Hazmat practice questions on hazard classes and key definitions in 49 CFR 171.8 and 173.2, each answer explained and linked to the rule.

questions.question: A shipper is deciding which hazard class to assign a material. Besides the definitional criteria of part 173, which provisions does the 171.8 definition of hazard class say the class is assigned under?

options.A: The packing group chosen by the carrier
options.C: The emergency response information on the shipping paper
options.D: The marking on the outer package

questions.explanation: 171.8 states: "Hazard class means the category of hazard assigned to a hazardous material under the definitional criteria of part 173 of this subchapter and the provisions of the § 172.101 table." The primary hazard is "the hazard class of a material as assigned in the § 172.101 table."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 171.8, Definitions and abbreviations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A material meets the defining criteria for more than one hazard class. Under the 171.8 definition of hazard class, how many hazard classes is it assigned to?

options.A: Every class whose criteria it meets
options.B: Two, a primary and a secondary class
options.C: None until the shipper obtains an approval

questions.explanation: Under 171.8, "A material may meet the defining criteria for more than one hazard class but is assigned to only one hazard class." Its other hazards are subsidiary hazards: "a hazard of a material other than the primary hazard."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 171.8, Definitions and abbreviations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A shipper needs the criteria for classifying a Division 5.1 oxidizer. Which section does the 173.2 table give for its definitions?
questions.explanation: In the 173.2 table, the Division 5.1 row reads "5.1 OXIDIZER" with "173.127" as the 49 CFR reference for definitions.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 173.2, Hazardous material classes and index to hazard class definitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Some rows of the 173.2 table show "None" in the class number column. What do those rows cover?
questions.explanation: The 173.2 table gives the class number "None" for "FORBIDDEN MATERIALS" (173.21) and "FORBIDDEN EXPLOSIVES" (173.54), and the section says the table lists definitions "for classifying hazardous materials, including forbidden materials."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 173.2, Hazardous material classes and index to hazard class definitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Which section does 171.8 point to for definitions relating to radioactive materials?
questions.explanation: 171.8 states: "Radioactive materials. See § 173.403 of this subchapter for definitions relating to radioactive materials."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 171.8, Definitions and abbreviations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: What counts as a hazardous material
questions.question: Under the 171.8 definition of hazardous material, who has determined that the substance or material is capable of posing an unreasonable risk to health, safety, and property when transported in commerce, and designated it as hazardous?

options.B: The shipper, by signing the shipper's certification
options.C: The motor carrier that accepts the material

questions.explanation: 171.8 states: "Hazardous material means a substance or material that the Secretary of Transportation has determined is capable of posing an unreasonable risk to health, safety, and property when transported in commerce, and has designated as hazardous under section 5103 of Federal hazardous materials transportation law".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 171.8, Definitions and abbreviations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: What counts as a hazardous material
questions.question: A material is listed in appendix A to 172.101. For it to be a hazardous substance under 171.8, what quantity condition must it meet?

options.A: The total on the vehicle must exceed 454 kg (1,001 pounds)
options.B: The shipment must contain at least ten packages
options.C: Any amount in any package is enough
options.D: Its quantity in one package must equal or exceed the reportable quantity (RQ) listed in appendix A

questions.explanation: A hazardous substance must be "in a quantity, in one package, which equals or exceeds the reportable quantity (RQ) listed in the appendix A to § 172.101 of this subchapter".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 171.8, Definitions and abbreviations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: What counts as a hazardous material
questions.question: A solution contains a material identified in appendix B to 172.101 as a severe marine pollutant. What concentration threshold by weight does the 171.8 marine pollutant definition set for it?
questions.explanation: The threshold is "One percent by weight of the solution or mixture for materials that are identified as severe marine pollutants in the appendix." Ten percent applies to other listed materials.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 171.8, Definitions and abbreviations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: What counts as a hazardous material
questions.question: A liquid with a flash point of 50 °C (122 °F) is intentionally heated and offered for transportation in a bulk packaging at 60 °C (140 °F). How does the 171.8 elevated temperature material definition apply?

options.A: It meets the definition, because it is a liquid with a flash point at or above 38 °C (100 °F) that is intentionally heated and offered at or above its flash point
options.B: It does not meet the definition, because a liquid must be at or above 100 °C (212 °F) in every case
options.C: It does not meet the definition, because only solids can be elevated temperature materials
options.D: It does not meet the definition, because the definition covers only non-bulk packagings

questions.explanation: An elevated temperature material, in a bulk packaging, includes one that "Is in a liquid phase with a flash point at or above 38 °C (100 °F) that is intentionally heated and offered for transportation or transported at or above its flash point".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 171.8, Definitions and abbreviations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: What counts as a hazardous material
questions.question: Under 171.8, which kind of hazardous material is left out of the definition of material of trade?

options.A: Material carried to support the operation or maintenance of the motor vehicle
options.B: Material carried to protect the health and safety of the operator or passengers
options.C: Material carried by a private motor carrier in direct support of a principal business other than transportation by motor vehicle

questions.explanation: 171.8 defines material of trade as "a hazardous material, other than a hazardous waste, that is carried on a motor vehicle" for one of three listed purposes, and the other three options are those purposes.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 171.8, Definitions and abbreviations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under the 171.8 definition, which of these can be a bulk packaging?

options.B: A transport vehicle or freight container in which hazardous materials are loaded with no intermediate form of containment
options.D: A packaging with a maximum capacity of 200 L (53 gallons) as a receptacle for a liquid

questions.explanation: Bulk packaging is "a packaging, other than a vessel or a barge, including a transport vehicle or freight container, in which hazardous materials are loaded with no intermediate form of containment." A liquid receptacle of "450 L (119 gallons) or less" is a non-bulk packaging.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 171.8, Definitions and abbreviations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: For a receptacle for a solid, what size condition does the 171.8 definition of bulk packaging set?

options.A: A water capacity greater than 454 kg (1000 pounds)
options.B: Either a maximum net mass greater than 400 kg (882 pounds) or any capacity
options.C: A maximum net mass greater than 400 kg (882 pounds) and a maximum capacity greater than 450 L (119 gallons)
options.D: A maximum capacity greater than 450 L (119 gallons), whatever its net mass

questions.explanation: For a solid, a bulk packaging has "A maximum net mass greater than 400 kg (882 pounds) and a maximum capacity greater than 450 L (119 gallons) as a receptacle for a solid". The water capacity test is for a gas.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 171.8, Definitions and abbreviations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A single consignor stacks four drums of a hazardous material on a pallet and secures them with stretch wrap for convenience in handling. What does 171.8 call the wrapped pallet load?
questions.explanation: An overpack is "an enclosure that is used by a single consignor to provide protection or convenience in handling of a package or to consolidate two or more packages", and examples include packages "Placed or stacked onto a load board such as a pallet and secured by strapping, shrink wrapping, stretch wrapping, or other suitable means". It "does not include a transport vehicle, freight container, or aircraft unit load device."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 171.8, Definitions and abbreviations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: How does the 171.8 definition of transport vehicle treat each cargo-carrying body, such as each trailer in a combination?

options.A: As one part of a single transport vehicle with the power unit
options.D: As a cargo tank, whatever its design

questions.explanation: 171.8 states: "Each cargo-carrying body (trailer, rail car, etc.) is a separate transport vehicle."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 171.8, Definitions and abbreviations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Which description matches the attachment condition in paragraph (2) of the 171.8 cargo tank definition?

options.A: The tank must be welded to the frame of a motor vehicle, with no other arrangement allowed
options.B: The tank must be lifted off the motor vehicle for loading and unloading
options.C: The tank must be fabricated under a specification for portable tanks
options.D: The tank is permanently attached to or forms part of a motor vehicle, or is not permanently attached but, by reason of its size, construction or attachment, is loaded or unloaded without being removed from the motor vehicle

questions.explanation: Paragraph (2) covers a tank that "Is permanently attached to or forms a part of a motor vehicle, or is not permanently attached to a motor vehicle but which, by reason of its size, construction or attachment to a motor vehicle is loaded or unloaded without being removed from the motor vehicle". Paragraph (3) excludes tanks "fabricated under a specification for" portable tanks, among others.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 171.8, Definitions and abbreviations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: As a condition of accepting a hazardous material, a carrier reviews the shipping papers and examines the packages. Under 171.8, does that make the carrier an offeror?

options.A: Yes. Reviewing a shipping paper is a pre-transportation function, so the carrier always becomes an offeror
options.B: No. A carrier is not an offeror when it performs a function required as a condition of acceptance
options.C: Yes, but only if the load is placarded
options.D: Yes, but only for bulk packagings

questions.explanation: 171.8 states: "A carrier is not an offeror when it performs a function required by this subchapter as a condition of acceptance of a hazardous material for transportation in commerce (e.g., reviewing shipping papers, examining packages".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 171.8, Definitions and abbreviations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Which self-employed person does the 171.8 definition of hazmat employee include?

options.A: No one. Only persons employed by a hazmat employer are hazmat employees
options.B: Only a self-employed person who holds a hazardous materials endorsement
options.C: Only a self-employed person who employs at least one other worker
options.D: An owner-operator of a motor vehicle transporting hazardous materials in commerce who in the course of self-employment directly affects hazardous materials transportation safety

questions.explanation: A hazmat employee includes a person who is "Self-employed (including an owner-operator of a motor vehicle, vessel, or aircraft) transporting hazardous materials in commerce who in the course of such self-employment directly affects hazardous materials transportation safety".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 171.8, Definitions and abbreviations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A State highway authority transports hazardous materials in commerce using its own employees. Under 171.8, can it be a hazmat employer?

options.A: Yes. The definition includes an authority of a State that transports hazardous materials in commerce
options.B: No. Only federal agencies are named in the definition
options.C: Only if it holds a special permit
options.D: No. Only private companies can be hazmat employers

questions.explanation: Paragraph (3) of the hazmat employer definition covers "A department, agency, or instrumentality of the United States Government, or an authority of a State, political subdivision of a State, or an Indian tribe" that, among other things, "Transports hazardous materials in commerce".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 171.8, Definitions and abbreviations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Before a shipment is offered, a shipper's employee determines the hazard class of the material. How does 171.8 classify that task?
questions.explanation: The 171.8 list of pre-transportation functions begins with "Determining the hazard class of a hazardous material." The three incidental-to-movement terms cover loading, storing and unloading the material in transportation.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 171.8, Definitions and abbreviations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: How does 171.8 treat storage of a hazardous material at its final destination as shown on a shipping document?

options.A: It counts as storage incidental to movement until the carrier leaves
options.B: It is not storage incidental to movement
options.C: It counts as loading incidental to movement
options.D: It counts as storage incidental to movement only for cargo tanks

questions.explanation: 171.8 states: "Storage incidental to movement does not include storage of a hazardous material at its final destination as shown on a shipping document."
